correctness.rationale: The pointwise Green representer solves -d^2g_x/ds^2=delta_x-ds/L with zero arclength mean; vertex Kirchhoff equations Qb=p-1/(2n) and layer-symmetric/antisymmetric modes give D=(n^2-1)/(24n)+h H_n/4, R_rung=h H_n and R_rail=1-1/(2n)-H_n/2. Edgewise diagonal A_n+(ell-R_uv-ell^2/L)t(1-t) then yields the submitted B coefficients and all equality representers. Both B coefficients are positive by the explicit Fourier-mode bound, so every edge maximum is its midpoint. For Delta_n=B_rung-B_rail, its derivative has n*(dDelta_n/dh)=sum_{k>0}F_h(a_k)-(h^2+4h+1)/(h+2)^2; F_h increasing in a and at least two a_k>=1 makes the first term >=2-1/(1+h)^2>=1 while the subtracted term is <1. Delta_n(0+)=-1/2, Delta_n(infty)>0, so unique h_n. The exact positive Poisson-kernel expression H_n=(1+q^n)/(sqrt(1+2h)(1-q^n)) yields strict n ordering, the h=1 n=3/4/5 boundary, golden root (1+sqrt5)/4, and implicit-function first correction (25+12sqrt5)/(95n). Independent numerical pseudoinverse comparisons across n=3,4,5,6,9 and h=1/3,1,5/2 gave 45 diagonal/curvature matches and independent threshold roots for n=3,4,5,10,20,100; these are bounded corroborations, not an infinite proof. The packaged Poisson checker was examined but not executed, and its 60-case output is not treated as proof.
